key_insight: AdHImEx is a hybrid implicit-explicit transport method that keeps second-order accuracy at large Courant numbers while needing only one matrix solve per time step.
engineering_relevance: It enables stable, mass-conservative advection for weather and climate models with better efficiency in mostly explicit flows and fewer accuracy losses in high-Courant regions.
method: Runge-Kutta AdImEx scheme blending third-order explicit stepping with Crank-Nicolson implicit stepping
Single sparse matrix solve per time step, even in the implicit regime
Stage-dependent divergence treatment to preserve constancy under spatially varying implicitness
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence, transport, and efficiency tests showing improved accuracy over prior first-order AdImEx schemes, low phase/amplitude error, and stable performance up to Courant numbers of 100.
watch_item: Implementation must carefully handle stage-dependent divergence and local implicitness on refined meshes to avoid spurious divergence or reduced accuracy.
paper_title: AdHImEx: Adaptively High-Order Implicit-Explicit Transport for Large Time Steps
